component.name: HS80 Control
component.summary: Control Corsair HS80 RGB Wireless through its supported receiver
Corsair HS80 RGB Wireless über kompatiblen Empfänger steuern

description.p: HS80 Control manages RGB zones, battery information, sleep timeout, sidetone and microphone gain for the Corsair HS80 RGB Wireless through receiver USB ID 1b1c:0a6b.

Headset product ID 0a69 is hardware-tested. Product ID 0a71 is experimental. HS80 MAX, HS80 RGB USB/wired, Xbox or Bluetooth variants, receivers with other USB IDs and multiple simultaneous receivers are not supported.
It can also create a PipeWire 7.1 virtual sink and render it to stereo with a user-selected SOFA HRTF.
The headset now announces microphone, charging cable and battery changes in German or English. The charging state no longer stays on after the cable is pulled.
The installer now quits a running application during an upgrade and starts the new version.

The interface is now available in German and English; the language is chosen at first start and can be changed on the overview page. New versions can be found and installed from within the application. A graphical installer for Fedora with KDE Plasma or GNOME is available.
The About dialog names Stickelbroeck Labs as the developer, with logo and website.

Lighting changes now apply live. Adds a colour-cycle mode, adjustable tempo, saved lighting profiles, a mute indicator with a free colour, and optional dimming at low battery. Effects use fewer frames to save battery.
Adds a system tray icon that shows the battery level. The app now starts minimised in the tray at login and stays there when its window is closed; both can be switched off on the overview page.
Adds a switch for the low-battery warning to the overview page. The warning stays on by default and can also be switched with hs80ctl battery-warning.
Warns with a desktop notification when the headset battery runs low, and again when it is almost empty. Connects to the headset right after login instead of up to a minute later.
Backs off instead of probing an unresponsive headset every two seconds.
Adds full support for the headset connected directly by USB cable, without the wireless receiver: battery, firmware, microphone state, lighting, sidetone and microphone gain.
Recognises a headset charging on its USB cable and explains that sound and controls run over the wireless receiver only.
Adds a reconnect button that rebuilds the receiver link and searches for the headset, and explains why no headset was found instead of leaving the status blank.
Fix the narrow-window switcher bar on libadwaita 1.9 and add system requirements, interface documentation and screenshots.
Redesigned as a native GNOME app: view switcher navigation, theme-aware cards and colors that follow the system style.
Explain muted-microphone lighting suppression and re-apply profiles on unmute.
Fix applying RGB profiles from the GTK interface on Fedora.
Fix hardware response matching and active headset discovery.
Initial implementation for receiver 1b1c:0a6b.
